title: Comprehensive policy models developed for EDPs

context_sources.name: Bruun, Sea-level rise as a cause of shore erosion, 1962
Stolper and Samuelson, Protection and Real Wages, 1941
World Bank, 140 million internal climate migrants by 2050

limitations: Most equations are embedded as vector graphics and reach the text as replacement glyphs.
The perception index and its probability thresholds are not on the same scale.
The culture-index update rule is never written, and the match is never applied to a winner.

tasks: Count people who lose land to the rising sea
Estimate who leaves because surroundings worsen
Project how fast a culture fades
Let people choose among leaving, accepting a plan, or waiting
Match them to an area and share the cost
Judge the effect on wages, industries and culture

section_map.summary: Two risk models, a culture simulation, three policy models, then wage and culture effects.
Sea-level danger and extreme weather, with the World Bank's 140 million by 2050.
Flooded population, a perception index, and a stochastic culture index for the Maldives.
Three choices for the displaced, a four-aspect match, and a fee that also steers emissions.
Short-run expansion with lower wages, long-run shift to the low end, three cultural futures.
The employment assumption is revised, and steady immigration is called essential.
Freedom on leaving, firmness on destination, fairness both ways, one controllable fee.
Clark, Bruun, Hofstede, Krugman, Stolper-Samuelson and the World Bank.

contributions.summary: Flooded population as an integral of a fitted density over the land the sea takes.
A fee whose single scale parameter sets global emissions because capital is held constant.
The short run expands both industries while the long run shrinks the high end.

dependency_graph.handoff: The people counted as flooded are the ones who must choose among the three options
The culture-loss horizon is why the match rewards cultural similarity and clustering
The chosen destination is the country whose wages and industries the inflow then shifts
Separating the fee from the match is what makes the chosen area willing to accept people

assumptions.summary: The island is round and people thin out evenly from the center.
Next year's cultural state depends only on this year.
Capital per person stays constant, and everyone maximizes.

data_and_preprocessing.summary: Maldives population, urban population and annual highest sea level from the World Bank and NOAA.
Six World Bank indicators and a CPIA rating, reduced by principal components.

models.summary: Exponential density plus coastal retreat, integrated over the flooded ring.
Six-indicator index with a piecewise probability of leaving.
Three-state culture chain with flooding shifted into the draw means.
Two-stage choice among three relocation options.
Four-aspect destination score with reported weights.
Fee on capital and emissions with a unique best response.
Two-sector specific-factor model at two horizons.

verification.summary: Maldives 2014 index is 62.66, read as the environment attracting rather than expelling.
A thousand culture simulations averaged, with 95 percent borders from the sample spread.

results_trace.summary: Culture to a tenth in 23 years, half-life 14 to 22 years, gone by about year 43 without protection.
Balanced emissions rise with capital at a diminishing rate and in fixed ratios across areas.
Wages fall in both horizons; the high-end industry grows only in the short run.

writing_logic.summary: People are split into those who must move and those who want to, and only the second group pays for housing.
The receiving country's objection is quoted before the fee is separated from the match.
The paper revises its own employment assumption once the wage result is in.

language_observations.summary: A test result that contradicts the expected pressure story is reported plainly.
Each inequality is immediately restated as what the person believes.
A cost declared too hard to judge is approached from the revenue side instead.
The favored outcome, pluralism, is given its own long-run danger.

judge_relevance_hypotheses.summary: Granting freedom on whether to leave but not on where to go respects both the person and the receiving country.
Separating who pays from who receives answers the refusal before it hardens.
Changing an earlier recommendation after seeing its cost reads as honesty rather than weakness.

weaknesses.summary: The Maldives index of 62.66 lies far outside the probability scale topped at 3.38.
The culture index has no written update rule, so its timelines cannot be reproduced.
The destination match is fully specified and then never used to name a winner.
The concavity proof says the capital exponent is negative, against its own stated range.

independent_extensions.summary: Reconcile the index units with the probability thresholds.
Write the rule that turns the three random draws into the next culture index.
Apply the four-aspect score to the Maldives and name the chosen area.

candidate_rule_impacts.summary: Standardize before comparing, and say when equal is better than greater.
Give each group its own option and its own charge, with the reason.

unresolved_questions.question: How can the Maldives index be 62.66 when departure is already certain below -2.825 and impossible above 3.38?
What operation combines the three random draws into the next culture index?
Which area does the match model actually select?
